speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing sudden onset abdominal pain; can you please describe exactly where the pain is located and how severe it is on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia.

The patient's sudden umbilical pain, recent history of acute myocardial infarction, and bloody diarrhea are highly suggestive of intestinal ischemia due to embolic or thrombotic occlusion of the mesenteric vessels. I will immediately request a CT angiogram of the abdomen to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdomen_CT_Angiography.
